writeup: TESS photometry has identified TIC 458507124 as a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 2.6947 days. The primary eclipse produces a dimming of 2.66%, detected with a signal-to-noise ratio of 47.8 using box least squares analysis. Pixel-level analysis confirms the signal at the target location, though with a centroid offset of 3.6 arcseconds and a peak signal-to-noise of 15.4 in difference imaging. No secondary eclipse was detected in the light curve. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a previously unknown object. The automated pipeline's machine-learning classifier assigns it a score of 0.32, indicating moderate confidence that this represents a real eclipsing binary rather than a false positive.
